mean: to adapt to circumstances as they arise
lit: to follow the moment and respond to the change

use.how: Predicate, often after 要, 学会, 靠, or as 随机应变的能力. Praises quick, sensible reactions when something unexpected happens.

near.diff: 入乡随俗 is adopting the customs of a place you go to; 随机应变 is reacting quickly to a sudden, unplanned turn of events.
顺其自然 is letting things take their course without stepping in; 随机应变 is actively changing what you do to meet the new situation.

cue: Halfway through your presentation the projector dies, and without missing a beat you carry on by sketching on the whiteboard. What skill did you show?

ctx.s: 出门旅行难免遇到意外，要学会{随机应变}。
ctx.en: Things inevitably go wrong when you travel; you have to learn to think on your feet.

ctx.s: 面试官突然换了个问题，好在她能{随机应变}，回答得很自然。
ctx.en: The interviewer suddenly switched questions, but luckily she could adapt on the spot and answered quite naturally.

ctx.s: 做销售这一行，{随机应变}的能力比背话术更重要。
ctx.en: In sales, being able to adapt in the moment matters more than memorising a script.

ctx.s: “演出时麦克风坏了怎么办？”“别慌，到时候{随机应变}。”
ctx.en: "What if the microphone breaks during the show?" "Don't panic, we'll deal with it as it comes."

ctx.s: 计划写得再详细也没用，真正上场还得靠{随机应变}。
ctx.en: However detailed the plan, once you are actually out there you have to rely on adapting as you go.

ctx.s: 导游发现山路被大雨冲断了，{随机应变}，把行程改成了参观博物馆。
ctx.en: Finding the mountain road washed out by heavy rain, the guide adapted at once and changed the trip to a museum visit.

bad.s: 到了日本就要{随机应变}，吃饭前也要说“我开动了”。
bad.en: (meant: in Japan you should follow local customs, like saying itadakimasu before meals)
bad.why: Following the habits of a place is rù xiāng suí sú; this idiom is reacting to a sudden change, not adopting local customs.

bad.s: 他这个人{随机应变}，今天说东明天说西，谁也不信他。
bad.en: (meant: he is fickle and keeps changing his story)
bad.why: It praises quick adaptation to events; it cannot criticise someone for being unreliable or inconsistent.

lit: the great task announces its completion

use.how: Predicate or exclamation, often with 终于 or 就…了: 终于大功告成了！ Said when a specific task or project is finished, from a big project to, playfully, a small chore.

near.diff: 功亏一篑 is failing at the very last step; 大功告成 is getting the whole job done.

cue: After weeks of redecorating, you hang the last picture on the wall, step back and smile. What do you announce?

ctx.s: 最后一道菜端上桌，{大功告成}！
ctx.en: The last dish is on the table, and we're done!

ctx.s: 我们装了一整天的书架，终于{大功告成}了。
ctx.en: We spent the whole day putting the bookcase together, and it's finally finished.

ctx.s: 论文改了五遍，今天交上去，总算{大功告成}。
ctx.en: I revised the thesis five times and handed it in today; at last the job is done.

ctx.s: “还差几条字幕没加，加完就{大功告成}了。”
ctx.en: "There are just a few subtitles left to add, and then the whole thing is done."

ctx.s: 别高兴得太早，数据还没核对，离{大功告成}还远着呢。
ctx.en: Don't celebrate too soon; the data hasn't been checked, and we're still far from finished.

ctx.s: 经过三年施工，这座跨江大桥的建设终于{大功告成}。
ctx.en: After three years of work, construction of the bridge across the river is finally complete.

bad.s: 他很有才华，年纪轻轻就{大功告成}，当上了总经理。
bad.en: (meant: he is talented and became general manager while still young)
bad.why: It marks the finishing of a particular task or project, not a person's success in life or career.

bad.s: 这个项目我们才开始，已经{大功告成}了一半。
bad.en: (meant: we have only just started and are already half done)
bad.why: It means the whole job is finished; it cannot be divided into fractions to describe partial progress.

lit: one's name is placed among the front grass flags, the vanguard

story.text: In the army of the state of Chu in the Spring and Autumn period, the scouts marching at the very front carried mao, a kind of tall grass, as their signal flag, raising it to warn the troops behind of danger. So qian mao, the front grass, meant the vanguard, and the Zuo Zhuan uses it in describing how the Chu army marched. Much later the phrase came to mean having one's name near the head of a list.

use.how: Predicate, usually after 在…中 or a place: 在全班名列前茅. Said of people or things in a ranking: exams, contests, sales, league tables.

near.diff: 首屈一指 means the very best, number one; 名列前茅 means somewhere among the top few of a ranking.

cue: Your cousin's exam results put her in the top three of her year group yet again. How do you describe where she stands?

ctx.s: 她学习很用功，每次考试都{名列前茅}。
ctx.en: She studies hard and is near the top in every exam.

ctx.s: 这款手机的销量在全国{名列前茅}。
ctx.en: This phone's sales are among the highest in the country.

ctx.s: 我们学校的篮球队在全市比赛中一直{名列前茅}。
ctx.en: Our school basketball team has always been one of the top teams in the city championships.

ctx.s: “你儿子成绩怎么样？”“还行，在班里算是{名列前茅}吧。”
ctx.en: "How are your son's grades?" "Not bad, he's more or less near the top of his class."

ctx.s: 这座城市的空气质量多年来在全省{名列前茅}。
ctx.en: For years this city's air quality has ranked among the best in the province.

ctx.s: 他刚转来时成绩倒数，一年后竟然{名列前茅}，老师都很惊讶。
ctx.en: When he transferred here he was near the bottom, yet a year later he was among the top, which amazed his teachers.

bad.s: 排队买票的时候，我{名列前茅}，很快就买到了。
bad.en: (meant: I was near the front of the queue, so I got a ticket quickly)
bad.why: It is about rank in results or standings, not about physical position in a line of people.

bad.s: 这次比赛他得了第一名，比第二名{名列前茅}很多。
bad.en: (meant: he won, far ahead of the runner-up)
bad.why: It states that someone is among the top; it cannot take a bǐ ... hěn duō comparison to say how far ahead they are.

mean: to ruin something by adding what is not needed
lit: to draw a snake and add feet

story.text: Servants in the state of Chu were given one jug of wine, too little to share, so they agreed that whoever drew a snake on the ground first would drink it. One man finished early and, showing off, started adding feet. Another finished his snake, took the jug and said: a snake has no feet, so yours is not a snake. The man who added the feet lost the wine.

use.how: Predicate or after 是, 就是, 反而: 再加一句就是画蛇添足。 Criticises an addition, done or proposed, that makes a finished thing worse.

near.diff: 多此一举 is any unnecessary extra step; 画蛇添足 says the extra addition actually spoils what was already good.
弄巧成拙 is any clever trick that backfires; 画蛇添足 is specifically adding something superfluous to a thing already complete.

cue: Your summary was clear and complete, but then you tacked on a long extra paragraph that only confused the readers. What did you do?

ctx.s: 这道菜已经很好吃了，再放糖就是{画蛇添足}。
ctx.en: This dish is already delicious; adding sugar would only spoil it.

ctx.s: 照片拍得很自然，加那么多滤镜反而{画蛇添足}。
ctx.en: The photo looks natural; piling on filters just ruins it.

ctx.s: “结尾再加一句总结怎么样？”“别，现在的结尾余味正好，再加就{画蛇添足}了。”
ctx.en: "How about adding a summary line at the end?" "Don't, the ending lingers just right as it is; adding more would spoil it."

ctx.s: 这幅山水画的留白恰到好处，他偏要在空白处题一首长诗，实在是{画蛇添足}。
ctx.en: The empty space in this landscape painting was just right, yet he insisted on writing a long poem across it; that really spoiled it.

ctx.s: 老街的木门本来很有味道，刷上亮漆以后，很多人觉得是{画蛇添足}。
ctx.en: The old street's wooden doors had real character; once they were coated in glossy paint, many people felt it had spoiled them.

ctx.s: 这部电影的结局本来很好，导演却又加了一段，有点{画蛇添足}。
ctx.en: The film's ending was good as it was, but the director tacked on an extra scene, which rather spoiled it.

bad.s: 她又帮我改正了几处错误，真是{画蛇添足}，太谢谢她了！
bad.en: (meant: she kindly corrected a few more mistakes for me, I'm so grateful)
bad.why: It criticises an addition that spoils something; it cannot be used to thank someone for useful extra work.

bad.s: 他做事总是很马虎，经常{画蛇添足}。
bad.en: (meant: he is careless and often leaves things out)
bad.why: It is about adding too much to something finished, not about carelessness or leaving things out.

mean: to wait idly for luck to strike again
lit: to keep watch by a tree stump, waiting for a hare

story.text: A farmer of the state of Song had a tree stump in his field. One day a running hare crashed into the stump, broke its neck and died. The farmer put down his plough and sat by the stump, hoping to get another hare. No hare ever came, and he became the laughing stock of Song. Han Feizi tells it to mock rulers who govern the present with the methods of the ancient kings.

use.how: Predicate, often with 不能, 别, or after 是: 只等客人上门是守株待兔。 Mocks waiting passively for a lucky chance, often one that happened once, instead of acting.

near.diff: 坐享其成 is enjoying the results of other people's work; 守株待兔 is waiting idly for a stroke of luck that may never come.

cue: A shop once got a big order from a stranger who wandered in; now the owner does no marketing at all and just sits waiting for another one. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 找工作不能{守株待兔}，要主动投简历。
ctx.en: You can't just sit and wait for a job to come to you; you have to send out your CV.

ctx.s: 开店只等客人上门是{守株待兔}，得想办法做宣传。
ctx.en: Running a shop and just waiting for customers to show up is waiting for luck; you have to find ways to advertise.

ctx.s: “这个客户上次是自己找来的，我们再等等吧。”“别{守株待兔}了，主动去联系。”
ctx.en: "This client found us on their own last time, let's just wait." "Stop waiting for lightning to strike twice, go and contact them."

ctx.s: 他中过一次小奖，就天天买彩票，等着再来一次，简直是{守株待兔}。
ctx.en: He won a small prize once, so now he buys lottery tickets every day waiting for it to happen again; it's pure wishful waiting.

ctx.s: 机会不会从天上掉下来，{守株待兔}的人只会越等越失望。
ctx.en: Opportunities don't fall from the sky; people who sit waiting for luck only grow more disappointed.

ctx.s: 去年有人在这条河边捡到过玉石，今年就有人天天来河边{守株待兔}。
ctx.en: Last year someone found a piece of jade by this river, and now people come every day to sit by the bank waiting for the same luck.

bad.s: 他每天早起锻炼，坚持了三年，真是{守株待兔}。
bad.en: (meant: he has kept up his morning exercise for three years, how persistent)
bad.why: It mocks idle waiting for luck; it cannot praise steady effort and perseverance.

bad.s: 我在门口{守株待兔}等朋友，他十分钟后就来了。
bad.en: (meant: I waited at the door for my friend, and he arrived ten minutes later)
bad.why: Waiting for someone who is on the way is ordinary waiting; the idiom is for hoping a lucky windfall will come while doing nothing.

mean: to talk to someone who can't appreciate it
lit: to play the zither to an ox

story.text: Gongming Yi, a musician of old, once played a refined melody on his zither to an ox. The ox went on grazing with its head down. It was not that the ox could not hear, but that the music did not suit its ears. Then he played sounds like the buzzing of mosquitoes and the lowing of a lost calf, and the ox flicked its tail, pricked up its ears and paced about, listening.

use.how: Predicate or after 是, 像: 跟他讲道理简直是对牛弹琴。 Mocks a listener who cannot understand or appreciate, or a speaker who ignores the audience. Rude if aimed at someone's face.

cue: You spent an hour explaining the beauty of a poem to a friend who only cares about football, and he just yawned the whole time. What were you doing?

ctx.s: 跟他讲古典音乐，简直是{对牛弹琴}。
ctx.en: Talking to him about classical music is a complete waste of breath.

ctx.s: 我跟室友讲了半天这部电影的镜头有多美，他只关心打斗场面，真是{对牛弹琴}。
ctx.en: I spent ages telling my roommate how beautiful the film's camerawork was, but he only cares about the fight scenes; it was completely lost on him.

ctx.s: “你又跟他讲道理了？”“别提了，{对牛弹琴}。”
ctx.en: "Did you try reasoning with him again?" "Don't ask, it went straight over his head."

ctx.s: 给小学生讲这么深的理论，不是{对牛弹琴}吗？
ctx.en: Isn't lecturing primary school kids on such advanced theory just talking over their heads?

ctx.s: 我说的话他一句也听不进去，再说下去也是{对牛弹琴}。
ctx.en: He doesn't take in a single word I say; going on would be pointless.

ctx.s: 讲课要看对象，不了解听众就开讲，难免{对牛弹琴}。
ctx.en: A lecture has to suit its audience; if you start without knowing your listeners, you are bound to be talking over their heads.

bad.s: 他钢琴弹得很好，在音乐会上{对牛弹琴}。
bad.en: (meant: he plays the piano well and performed at the concert)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with playing well; it means talking to people who cannot appreciate it, so here it insults the concert audience.

bad.s: 王教授，谢谢您今天给我们{对牛弹琴}，我们学到了很多。
bad.en: (meant: thank you, Professor Wang, for teaching us today)
bad.why: It calls the listeners oxen; as a thank-you it insults both the audience and the speaker.

mean: a person with a narrow view of the world
lit: a frog at the bottom of a well

story.text: A frog living in a shallow, broken-down well boasted to a great turtle from the Eastern Sea about how happy it was there, and invited the turtle in. Before the turtle could get its left foot in, its right knee was stuck. The turtle backed away and told the frog about the sea: so vast that floods and droughts never change its level. Hearing this, the frog was startled and at a loss.

use.how: A noun phrase, after 是, 像 or 做: 别做井底之蛙。 Criticises someone, often oneself, whose outlook is narrow and who thinks their little world is all there is.

near.diff: 一知半解 is shallow knowledge of one subject; 井底之蛙 is a person whose whole view of the world is narrow without knowing it.

cue: A man who has never left his hometown insists its little river is the greatest in the world and laughs at anyone who mentions the sea. What is he?

ctx.s: 多出去走走，别做{井底之蛙}。
ctx.en: Get out and see the world; don't be a frog in a well.

ctx.s: 出国留学以后，我才发现自己以前就是个{井底之蛙}。
ctx.en: It was only after going abroad to study that I realised how narrow my view of the world had been.

ctx.s: 他以为自己的公司是全国最好的，真是{井底之蛙}。
ctx.en: He thinks his company is the best in the country; he really has no idea what's out there.

ctx.s: “我们镇上的菜最好吃！”“你呀，就是只{井底之蛙}，去大城市看看吧。”
ctx.en: "Our town has the best food anywhere!" "You're a frog in a well, you know; go and see a big city."

ctx.s: 只看一种新闻、只听一种声音，人很容易变成{井底之蛙}。
ctx.en: If you read only one kind of news and hear only one voice, you can easily end up with a very narrow view of the world.

ctx.s: 这家企业多年不关注行业变化，像{井底之蛙}一样，不知道国外的技术早就超过了自己。
ctx.en: For years the company ignored changes in its industry; like a frog in a well, it never knew that foreign technology had long since overtaken it.

bad.s: 他对这道数学题不太懂，是个{井底之蛙}。
bad.en: (meant: he doesn't really understand this maths problem)
bad.why: It describes a narrow outlook on the whole world, not failing to understand one particular thing; for that say bú tài dǒng.

bad.s: 他很{井底之蛙}，什么都不知道。
bad.en: (meant: he is very narrow-minded and knows nothing)
bad.why: It is a noun phrase and cannot take hěn like an adjective; put shì or xiàng before it instead.

lit: one's own spear and shield clash

story.text: A man of the state of Chu was selling shields and spears. Praising his shields, he said they were so strong that nothing could pierce them. Praising his spears, he said they were so sharp that there was nothing they could not pierce. Someone asked: what happens if you use your spear to strike your shield? The man had no answer.

use.how: Predicate, often with 前后 or after 这不是…吗: 他的说法前后自相矛盾。 Said of one person's or one text's words or actions that cannot both be true.

near.diff: 口是心非 is saying one thing while meaning the opposite; 自相矛盾 is two things someone says or does that cannot both be true.

cue: A witness first says he was at home all evening, then mentions seeing the accident happen on the street that night. What is wrong with his account?

ctx.s: 你刚说没去过，现在又说去过，这不是{自相矛盾}吗？
ctx.en: You just said you'd never been, and now you say you have; aren't you contradicting yourself?

ctx.s: 这份报告前后{自相矛盾}，数据根本对不上。
ctx.en: This report contradicts itself; the figures simply don't match up.

ctx.s: 他一边说要省钱，一边天天买奶茶，真是{自相矛盾}。
ctx.en: He says he wants to save money, yet he buys bubble tea every day; it makes no sense.

ctx.s: 嫌疑人的口供{自相矛盾}，警察认为他在撒谎。
ctx.en: The suspect's statement contradicted itself, and the police believed he was lying.

ctx.s: “主角前面说自己是独生子，后面又提到他哥哥。”“作者写得{自相矛盾}了。”
ctx.en: "Early on the hero says he's an only child, then later his brother turns up." "The author has contradicted himself."

ctx.s: 这项规定既要求准时下班，又要求当天工作必须做完，本身就{自相矛盾}。
ctx.en: The rule requires leaving on time but also finishing all of the day's work; it contradicts itself.

bad.s: 我和妹妹的意见{自相矛盾}，吵了一架。
bad.en: (meant: my sister and I disagreed and had a row)
bad.why: Zì xiāng means contradicting oneself; two people disagreeing is yìjiàn bù hé or yǒu máodùn.

bad.s: 他心里很{自相矛盾}，不知道该选哪份工作。
bad.en: (meant: he feels torn about which job to choose)
bad.why: Feeling torn is xīnli hěn máodùn or zuǒ yòu wéi nán; this idiom is about statements or actions that clash.

mean: to fix the problem after a loss, before it worsens
lit: to mend the pen after losing sheep

story.text: Zhuang Xin warned King Xiang of Chu that his life of pleasure would ruin the state, but the king would not listen and Zhuang Xin left. Soon Qin took the Chu capital and the king fled. He sent for Zhuang Xin and asked what could still be done. Zhuang Xin replied: to call the dog after seeing the hare is not too late; to mend the pen after losing sheep is not too late either.

use.how: Predicate or after 算是, 叫: 换了新锁，也算亡羊补牢。 Often with 为时未晚. Said approvingly of fixing the cause after a loss so it does not happen again.

near.diff: 后悔莫及 is regret that comes too late to help; 亡羊补牢 is acting after a loss to stop it happening again.

cue: After their flat was burgled, a family finally fits strong locks and an alarm so it can't happen again. How might a neighbour describe this, approvingly?

ctx.s: 家里被偷了一次，他马上换了新锁，也算{亡羊补牢}。
ctx.en: After his home was burgled, he changed the locks straight away; better late than never.

ctx.s: 这次考试没考好不要紧，{亡羊补牢}，为时未晚。
ctx.en: Don't worry about doing badly this time; if you fix what went wrong now, it's not too late.

ctx.s: 电脑坏了丢了很多文件，从那以后他每周都备份，这叫{亡羊补牢}。
ctx.en: His computer broke and he lost a lot of files; since then he backs up every week, which is learning from the loss.

ctx.s: “公司已经被罚款了，现在加强管理还有用吗？”“{亡羊补牢}总比什么都不做强。”
ctx.en: "The company has already been fined; is tightening management any use now?" "Fixing it after the fact is better than doing nothing."

ctx.s: 事故发生后，学校连夜检查了所有教室的电线，及时{亡羊补牢}。
ctx.en: After the accident, the school checked the wiring in every classroom overnight, fixing the problem before anything worse could happen.

ctx.s: 有些问题等出了事再{亡羊补牢}，代价就太大了，不如提前预防。
ctx.en: With some problems, waiting until something goes wrong before fixing them costs far too much; better to prevent them in advance.

bad.s: 下周要下雨，我们今天先{亡羊补牢}，把屋顶修好。
bad.en: (meant: it will rain next week, so let's fix the roof today in advance)
bad.why: It needs a loss that has already happened; preparing before any damage is wèi yǔ chóu móu.

bad.s: 他错过了最后一班车，只能{亡羊补牢}，后悔得要命。
bad.en: (meant: he missed the last bus and could only regret it bitterly)
bad.why: It is about acting to prevent further loss, not regretting what cannot be undone; that is hòu huǐ mò jí.

mean: to spoil things by forcing them to grow too fast
lit: to pull up seedlings to help them grow

story.text: A man of the state of Song worried that his seedlings were growing too slowly, so he went into the field and pulled each one up a little. He came home worn out and told his family: I am exhausted today, I have been helping the seedlings grow. His son ran out to look, and the seedlings had all withered. Mencius tells the story to warn against forcing what must grow naturally.

use.how: Predicate or after 是, 无异于: 这是拔苗助长。 Criticises pushing a child, a person or an undertaking to develop faster than it can, so that it is harmed. Also written 揠苗助长.

near.diff: 急于求成 is being impatient for results in general; 拔苗助长 is actively forcing something to develop and so damaging it.

cue: Parents make their small son study all evening, every evening, so he will get ahead, and soon he hates books. What have they done?

ctx.s: 孩子才三岁就学四门外语，这是{拔苗助长}。
ctx.en: Making a three-year-old learn four foreign languages is forcing him far too fast.

ctx.s: 学习要一步一步来，{拔苗助长}只会适得其反。
ctx.en: Learning has to go step by step; pushing too fast only backfires.

ctx.s: “我想让他跳两级，早点上大学。”“别{拔苗助长}，他还没准备好。”
ctx.en: "I want him to skip two years and get to university early." "Don't force it, he isn't ready."

ctx.s: 新员工才来一个月就让他当经理，不是{拔苗助长}吗？
ctx.en: Making a new hire a manager after just one month, isn't that pushing him before he's ready?

ctx.s: 有些家长给孩子报了太多补习班，结果{拔苗助长}，孩子反而讨厌学习了。
ctx.en: Some parents sign their children up for too many tutoring classes, and by forcing them they make the children hate studying.

ctx.s: 专家认为，用大量补贴逼着新产业快速扩张，无异于{拔苗助长}。
ctx.en: Experts argue that using huge subsidies to force a new industry to expand quickly is no different from pulling up seedlings to make them grow.

bad.s: 他学习很努力，成绩进步得很快，真是{拔苗助长}。
bad.en: (meant: he works hard and his grades improved quickly)
bad.why: It criticises forcing growth in a way that does harm; fast progress that comes naturally is not described this way.

bad.s: 时间不多了，我们得{拔苗助长}，赶快出发。
bad.en: (meant: time is short, we must hurry and set off)
bad.why: It is not a word for hurrying; it describes damaging something by pushing its development too fast.
